bullets.text: Companywide CR improved 0.9 points YOY; Personal Lines CR was 95.1 (1.1 points better); Commercial Lines CR was 89.5; Property CR was 127.5; revised profitability expectations led to a ~$225M goodwill write-off.
Raised personal auto rates averaging 6% across 17 states representing ~40% of trailing 12-month premium; countrywide net rate increases were just over 2% for Q2 and 9% YTD.
PL PIF fell 1% YOY to 17.2M auto and 5.5M special lines, ending a 20+ year growth streak; CL PIF grew 12% to surpass the 1M policy milestone.
Companywide NPW +8% YOY; CL NPW grew 16% alongside strong core commercial auto and telematics expansion; PL NPW increased 6%; Property NPW grew 8%.

Hail and adverse weather contributed about 3 points to quarterly PL CR; Property suffered 41 points of catastrophe losses from thunderstorms, hail, and tornadoes; claim settlement severity inflation persisted.

Portfolio total return was -3.6%; fixed income returned -2.4% caused by higher interest rates and wider credit spreads; equities returned -16.3% (~5% of portfolio); Progressive continues to believe a conservative posture is appropriate.

Personal auto model 8.7 reached 28 states (~65% countrywide premium) with model 8.8 launching in Iowa; BOP expanded into 37th state; Heavy Truck Roadside Assistance deployed in four additional states.

Growth headwinds emerged in for-hire transportation as freight markets softened and overall economic activity slowed; financial conditions tightened as the Federal Reserve raised interest rates and initiated quantitative tightening.

Property remains a foundational building block of the Destination strategy; Progressive is taking deliberate actions to diversify geographic concentration into less volatile states representing over 40% of the U.S. property market.

Celebrated 85th anniversary with CEO small-group lunches for 150+ employees and a 'Big Wish' program receiving 9,000+ submissions; emphasized living Core Values and the Golden Rule during difficult times.
